description: Write paychecks into the document — **several in one call**, one entry per paycheck. Each needs the salary month, the payment date, gross and net; an itemization is optional, and each of its lines names a deduction type by id from `paychecks`. Read a paycheck PDF or photo yourself and this is where what it says goes. **Dry-runs by default**: it returns what it would record, including whether each paycheck’s itemization reconciles to its net, and writes nothing until called again with commit true. Nothing here deduplicates — a second paycheck for a salary month is allowed, because a 13th salary is exactly that. The document is copied to a timestamped .bak before anything is written.

commit.description: Default false. False previews the batch; true writes it.

path.description: Absolute path to a .emd file on this machine.

paychecks.description: One entry per paycheck. Up to 60 in a call.

employer_name.description: Which employer. Needed only when the user has more than one.

gross.description: Gross pay in major units, as the paycheck prints it.

is_irregular.description: True for a 13th salary or a bonus month, which averages then leave out. Only ever on the user’s say-so.

lines.description: The itemization. Every line names a deduction type by id; `paychecks` prints the vocabulary. Anything the list cannot express goes on `ded:other` with a note.

basis_amount.description: The salary base a percentage applied to, where the paycheck prints one.

deduction_type_id.description: An id from the vocabulary `paychecks` prints.

employee_amount.description: What came off the employee’s side, in major units, as a **magnitude** — the paycheck prints no minus and neither should this. 0 is a real answer.

employer_amount.description: The employer’s share of the same line, where the paycheck states one. Leave it out when the type has no employer side at all — that is a different fact from a share of zero.

note.description: What the paycheck called this line, when it is not obvious.

net.description: Net pay in major units. **Entered, never computed** — the app does not argue with the paycheck.

note.description: Anything about this paycheck worth keeping — a retroactive correction, say.

payment_date.description: The day the money landed, as YYYY-MM-DD.

period.description: The **salary month** as YYYY-MM — the month the pay is for, not the month it was paid in.

name: record_paychecks
title: Record paychecks
